# **Incident report**

## **Summary**

On September 1, an issue with an underlying service used by Voyado caused parts of the platform to stop working as expected.

The issue affected Abandoned Cart, the Revenue Overview Dashboard, new Analytics reports, and the Automation Overview Dashboard for all tenants using these features.

We identified the cause and implemented a fix that restored the affected functionality.

## **Customer impact**

During the incident, customers using the affected features experienced errors or were unable to access the expected information.

The following features were affected:

* Abandoned Cart
* Revenue Overview Dashboard
* New Analytics reports
* Automation Overview Dashboard

No customer data was lost, modified, or exposed as a result of the incident.

## **Root Cause**

The incident was caused by a change made to an underlying service that Voyado uses to retrieve information for these features.

The change altered what information was available to Voyado. This prevented the affected features from retrieving the information they needed to operate correctly.

## **Mitigation**

Once we identified the cause, we adjusted our service to work with the change and restored the affected functionality.

We also added safeguards to better handle this type of situation should it occur again.

## **Next steps**

We are reviewing how we use the underlying service to make the affected functionality less sensitive to similar changes in the future.

We are also improving our monitoring so that failures affecting these features can be detected and addressed more quickly.

## Summary

On July 7, 2026, between approximately 14:50 and 16:32 CEST, some Engage customers experienced degraded platform performance. This included slow response times, timeouts, and intermittent error messages.

The issue was caused by an infrastructure event that temporarily affected the platform’s ability to process requests as expected.

The incident was fully resolved at 16:32 CEST, and performance returned to normal.

## Customer impact

During the incident, affected customers may have experienced slower than normal response times, request timeouts, and intermittent error messages when using Engage.

The impact was limited to parts of the platform, and no customer data was lost.

## Root cause

The incident was triggered by an infrastructure event in one part of the platform. This led to an increased number of queued requests and higher load than normal.

To protect the overall stability of the platform, an automatic protective mechanism was activated. In this case, the mechanism also affected some customers who were indirectly impacted by the original event, which made the issue more noticeable.

## Mitigation

Once the issue was identified, we added more capacity to help the platform process the increased load and reduce the queue of requests.

When the load returned to normal, the protective mechanism was lifted for affected customers. Performance then recovered, and the incident was resolved.

## Next steps

We are reviewing how similar infrastructure events are handled by the platform, with the goal of reducing the risk of increased load building up in the future.

We are sorry for the disruption this caused and appreciate your patience while we worked to restore normal platform performance.

### Summary

On Friday, May 22, between approximately 11:15 and 12:45 CEST, users experienced issues when opening the Design Studio in Engage to list send-out messages.

Message sending was not impacted. Scheduled send-outs, automation send-outs, and message delivery to recipients continued to work as expected.

The issue was resolved after deploying a hotfix to the affected frontend services.

### Customer impact

Customers using Design Studio in Engage were affected, the classic email editor was not impacted. During the incident, affected users could experience problems with:

* Viewing existing send-outs
* Working with send-outs
* Opening the Design Studio

There was no impact on recipients or outbound message delivery.

### Root cause

The issue was caused by a recent frontend change related to new functionality in Engage. A component connected to this new functionality resulted in an issue failing to load the send-out list and Design studio.

### Mitigation

Internal and external reports about the issue was notified to the Engineering team who started investigating immediately. The affected area was quickly identified, and a hotfix was prepared.

The fix was then deployed to the affected frontend services in batches to reduce risk. The fix was verified during the deployment and the incident was resolved at approximately 12:45 CEST.

### Next steps

We are reviewing both technical safeguards and release routines to reduce the risk of similar incidents.

We apologize for the disruption this caused for affected users and thank you for your patience while we worked on the resolution.

incidents.body:
**Summary**    
Between April 7 and April 9, 2026, parts of the Voyado platform experienced degraded performance related to one of our database clusters.    
The issue caused slower response times and intermittent errors in affected parts of the platform, including our APIs and some connected background processing. We took immediate action to reduce the load, mitigate customer impact, and restore stability.    
Customers that were most affected by the database load were promptly moved to other database clusters, which resolved the issue for those customers.

**Customer impact**    
Customers connected to the affected database cluster may have experienced degraded performance, including slow or failing API requests, delays in background processing, and intermittent issues in some platform functionality.    
During the most affected periods, the increased load also impacted shared platform services, which led to slower API response times for some customers outside the affected database cluster.

**Root Cause**    
Our investigation is still ongoing. Current findings point to the performance and functionality of a specific database cluster as the main contributing factor. We are continuing the investigation together with experts from our database vendor to isolate the underlying root cause.

**Mitigation**    
We acted immediately to reduce the impact and stabilize the platform. This included reducing load on the affected cluster, performing operational failovers, and moving affected customers to other database clusters.    
Customers that were moved to other clusters were no longer affected by the issue after the move. These actions helped restore platform stability while the investigation continued.

**Next steps**    
We are continuing the root cause investigation together with our vendor’s specialists to fully understand why this specific database cluster degraded.    
In parallel, we are reviewing monitoring and alerting around database performance and related platform services, so that similar patterns can be detected and acted on even earlier in the future.

  
We apologize for the inconvenience this incident may have caused and appreciate your understanding.

## Summary

On the afternoon of 20 March, we experienced a disruption affecting Vipps and Treazure integrations. The investigation showed that the issue was caused by a very large burst of webhook-triggering updates from one customer workflow. The issue was mitigated the same day by disabling the affected workflow, after which service returned to normal.

## Customer Impact

Multiple customers experienced failed or interrupted external API call activities connected to Vipps flows, and some impact was also seen in Treazure flows. This resulted in timeouts and failed processing during the incident window.

## Root Cause

The incident was caused by a massive simultaneous burst of webhook-triggering updates from one customer workflow, which overloaded the shared integration service. This created performance issues in the integration layer and affected Vipps and Treazure integrations using the same service.

## Mitigation

After the source of the traffic spike was identified, the affected webhook endpoint was disabled and the customer integration with Treazure was temporarily deactivated. This reduced the load on the integration service and restored normal behaviour for other tenants.

## Next Steps

To reduce the risk of similar incidents in the future, we are:

* Reviewing throttling and rate-limiting for webhook traffic
* Reviewing monitoring and alerting for the integration 
* Strengthening guidance and communication around high-volume customer automations

We apologize for the inconvenience this incident may have caused and appreciate your understanding.

incidents.body:
## Summary

On March 15th 2026, an issue affecting Delta Share was identified. The issue was caused by a change in how timestamp values were stored. This change was introduced as part of an infrastructure upgrade on March 13, 2026. The incident was limited in scope and, based on our investigations, only one tenant/partner was affected.

## Customer impact

One tenants/partners Delta Share integration failed when loading data containing timestamp fields. This meant that some shared data could not be processed correctly in their integration. At this time, no other Delta Share users have been identified as affected.

## Root cause

As part of an upgrade, the infrastructure used to prepare shared data was moved to a newer cluster setup. Following this change, timestamp values were written in a different format than before. While the data itself remained correct and available, one partner integration was not able to handle the new timestamp format.

## Mitigation

We worked directly with the partner that was affected by the issue after the issue was reported. The partner updated their integration to support the new timestamp format, which resolved the issue. We also evaluated whether to revert to the previous format, but decided not to do so since no other users appeared to be affected and a rollback would have required significant additional work for the impacted partner.

## Next steps

To reduce the risk of similar issues in the future, we are taking the following actions:

* Evaluating validation of data types when making infrastructure changes

We are sorry for the inconvenience this caused.

## Summary

On the afternoon of February 5th, we experienced a disruption affecting the delivery of app push notifications for customers using the Vipps integration. The issue was caused by an expired security certificate in a third-party integration service. The problem was identified and resolved the same day, and all delayed events were sent shortly after recovery.

## Customer impact

Some customers experienced **delayed app push notifications**.  
No notifications were lost, and no other functionality within the Voyado platform was affected. The impact was considered minor and non-critical.

## Root cause

The issue was caused by an **expired security certificate** used by a third-party integration service that handles communication between Voyado Engage and Vipps. Once the certificate expired, event delivery was temporarily blocked.

## Mitigation

After identifying the expired certificate, a new certificate was issued and applied with support from our IT team. Once the integration was restored, **all queued events were successfully sent**. Vipps was informed after resolution.

## Next steps

To reduce the risk of similar incidents in the future, we are:

* Improving monitoring and alerting for the integration to detect issues earlier
* Establishing clearer ownership and reminders for certificate renewals well ahead of expiration

We apologize for the inconvenience this delay may have caused and appreciate your understanding.

## Summary

On December 30th, a performance issue on one of our servers led to delayed API response times for a subset of customers. The issue was quickly identified and mitigated within approximately one hour.

## Customer Impact

The delays affected API responses for customers hosted on one specific server. All other parts of the platform remained fully functional.

## Root Cause

The issue was triggered by a large import job that attempted to process a high volume of transactions in a single run. This created a significant number of internal locks in our database, leading to degraded performance. 

## Remediation & Prevention 

Once the problematic job was identified, it was stopped, and a work-around was made to prevent further issues.

## Next Steps

We are reviewing the job and do necessary changes to safe-guard how the platform handles high-volume imports, reducing the risk of similar incidents in the future.

We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this caused and appreciate your patience while we worked to resolve the issue. Preventing disruptions like this remains a top priority, and we are committed to learning from this incident to improve platform resilience.

incidents.body:
### Summary

On the morning of November 28, we experienced a delay in the systems responsible for processing message statistics in Voyado Engage. While message delivery worked as expected, statistics—such as opens, clicks, and bounces—were shown with a delay of up to 60 minutes in the user interface.

### Customer Impact

* Message delivery was not affected.
* Users saw delays of up to 60 minutes when reviewing delivery statistics for email send-outs.
* Segmentation based on message statistics continued to work, though with a delay.
* This affected all customers using Engage to send messages during the morning and early afternoon, the impact was isolated to a delay in viewing the statistics for the messages sent.

### Root Cause

The issue was caused by limitations in how our internal message handler for message statistics in particular is scaled during high load. Specifically, the service handling statistics did not automatically increase its capacity as expected due to how scaling logic was configured. 

### Mitigation

* Manual scaling was applied to increase processing capacity.
* Services were restarted to resolve blocks in the processing.
* We adjusted the internal message handling strategy to improve throughput.
* By mid-afternoon, statistics processing had caught up and delays were resolved.

### Next Steps

* Review and update scaling configuration to ensure automatic scaling behaves as expected.

We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience this may have caused and appreciate your patience while we worked to resolve the issue.

## Summary

On November 7th, an unusually high number of internal events were generated due to a planned feature rollout. This caused delays in processing certain automations.

## Customer Impact

Automations triggered by customer interactions or audience targeting were delayed by up to 12 hours. All affected automations were eventually executed. Other parts of the platform operated as normal.

## Root Cause and Mitigation

When the new Marketing Groups feature was enabled for all customers, a large volume of events \(hundreds of millions\) was generated in a short time. The system processing these events could not keep up, which resulted in delays for other events in the same internal queue.

To restore normal flow, we temporarily cleared out the backlog of non-critical events and performed database synchronizations to ensure data accuracy. Normal operation resumed later the same day.

## Next Steps

We are improving our monitoring and alerting to detect similar issues earlier, and we are reviewing our event handling capacity and release procedures to prevent future impact from large-scale rollouts.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your patience while we resolved the issue.

incidents.body:
**Description**

During an A/B test of personalization functionality, an update introduced data that was not compatible with older system versions. This caused search-page errors for some shoppers when their requests were routed between nodes running different versions. 

The A/B test was disabled promptly, preventing new incompatible data from being written. This action significantly reduced the error rate. Errors continued to occur for a limited number of shoppers who had already been affected, until all older nodes were fully upgraded.  

* The majority of customers running the test experienced no impact. 

* Most customers faced none or a few errors. 

All systems were upgraded to the new version, eliminating the incompatibility and restoring full stability. 

**Business impact**

* Some shoppers attempting searches received error messages, which could disrupt their browsing and purchase flow. 

* Only customers actively running the personalization A/B test were affected. For most, the number of shoppers impacted was very limited. 

**Review**

* Review of rollout and A/B testing procedures to reduce cross-version risk. 

* Improve error handling in personalization so that issues cannot cause shopper-facing failures. 

* Add faster “kill switch” capabilities to disable personalization in case of future incidents.

incidents.body:
### Summary

Between October 7th and October 8th, users could experience delays in the display of message send-out status updates in the Engage interface. While the messages were sent as expected, the visual feedback in the interface did not reflect their actual status.

### Customer Impact

During the incident, message send-out status and related statistics were delayed in Engage. No messages were lost or failed to send—this was a display issue only.

### Root Cause

The delay was caused by an unusually large batch of events from our data processing pipeline that overwhelmed an internal message handler. The large batch occurred due to a change in configuration during refactoring that led to unintentionally re-sending of all historic events. While the initial ingestion layer could handle the load, the downstream system could not process events fast enough, resulting in a backlog. A key process responsible for moving events downstream stopped functioning correctly, and the issue went unnoticed for several hours adding to the backlog and ultimate delay.

### Mitigation

* Redundant subscriptions were removed and recreated to clear the backlog.
* Processing power was increased for the affected message handler.
* The rate of downstream event processing was reduced to alleviate pressure.
* Event processing was monitored until the backlog was fully cleared.

By the afternoon of October 8th, the system had fully caught up and normal status updates were visible again in Engage.

### Next Steps

To reduce the risk of similar issues occurring in the future, we are implementing the following improvements:

* Improving autoscaling for the internal message handler system
* Improving safeguards in our data platform to avoid overwhelming downstream systems
* Adding delivery time monitoring to our internal dashboards to detect delays earlier

We apologize for the inconvenience this may have caused and appreciate your patience while we worked to resolve the issue.

# **Summary**

  
On October 1st, 2025, the Order V3 API was unavailable between 12:00 and 14:30 CEST. The issue was caused by a faulty update intended to handle previously failed orders and led to serialization errors that made the API unresponsive. The problem was identified and a fix was deployed to restore normal operations.

# **Customer Impact**

  
A few customers were affected during the incident. Customers using the Order V3 API were unable to place or manage orders through this version of the API during the downtime. Other versions and platform features remained unaffected.

# **Root Cause**

  
The issue derived from a serialization error introduced during a fix deployment aimed at resending failed order messages. This error caused all incoming commands to fail, rendering the Order V3 API temporarily unusable.

# **Mitigation**

  
The issue was identified and a fix was prepared and deployed. Full functionality was restored by 14:30 CEST, the system was closely monitored to ensure stability.

# **Next Steps**

  
We are taking several actions to prevent similar incidents:

* Improving test coverage and automated validation for critical API updates.
* Enhancing our developer tools to better simulate and detect serialization issues.

We apologize for the inconvenience caused and appreciate your patience as we continue to improve the reliability of our platform.

## Summary

On September 30th, Engage experienced a temporary disruption in email send-outs due to an error in newly deployed code. The issue was quickly identified, and a hotfix was deployed. While no messages were lost, some email messages were delayed as the system worked through a backlog.

## Customer Impact

Majority of customers were potentially affected. Most experienced delays in automation emails. In a few cases, delays were up to 8 hours, but the majority of impacted messages were delivered within 3–4 hours. No SMS or priority messages were affected.

## Root Cause

The disruption was caused by an internal misconfiguration in how the platform determined where to store and retrieve data for email messages. When a new code deployment corrected this configuration, it unintentionally disrupted messages that had already been processed using the old setup. This led to messages being queued and not sent.

## Mitigation

After identifying the issue, a hotfix was deployed to prevent further impact. Additional work was done throughout the day to manually resend affected messages and ensure all queued messages were successfully delivered.

## Next Steps

To reduce the risk of similar issues in the future, we are:

* Implementing automated code checks that will detect and block misconfigurations before deployment.
* Improving internal processes for incident handling and maintenance tooling, including procedures to quickly resending impacted messages.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your patience while we resolved the issue.

## Summary

On September 28th, Engage experienced delays in sending bulk email messages. The issue was caused by part of our internal email processing setup not operating as expected. The delay was resolved the same day, and no messages were lost.

## Customer Impact

Bulk emails for a minor sub-set of customers were delayed by up to 3 hours. Priority messages, including automation emails and SMS, were not affected and were delivered as normal.

## Root Cause

Three of the internal services responsible for processing emails were not active due to a system update on September 27th. This caused them to restart without automatically reactivating the needed components. Combined with a high traffic in the system, this led to a backlog in the email messaging pipeline.

## Mitigation

The inactive services were redeployed, restoring full processing capacity. Once this was done, the message queue was quickly processed, and operations returned to normal.

## Next Steps

To prevent similar issues in the future, we are:

* Updating our deployment pipeline to ensure the required components are automatically restarted after updates.
* Introducing additional monitoring and alerts to detect inactive or underperforming internal services sooner.

We appreciate your understanding and patience while we worked through this issue and apologize for any inconvenience.

incidents.title: [Engage] System Performance Degradation

incidents.body:
### Summary

On the morning of September 17th, the Engage platform experienced degraded performance primarily affecting messaging and APIs. The root cause was traced to a scenario triggered by the intentional disabling of messaging functionality for a specific tenant. This caused an unusually high load on our infrastructure, causing ripple effects in parts of the system affecting other tenants as well.

### Customer Impact

* **Messaging delays** of 10–30 minutes for most customers. One tenant experienced longer delays \(up to 60 minutes\) and required minor manual intervention for a small number of messages.
* **APIs affected**: CreateContact, GetContact, and UpdateContact showed poor response times for a sub-set of customers. 

No messages were lost, and all systems were fully recovered by 11:10 CEST.

### Root Cause

The incident stemmed from disabling messaging functionality for a specific tenant in combination with messaging activity for that tenant. This generated a lot of activity in the system among other triggering a poorly optimized database query. The query caused significant load on our database servers, leading to cascading delays across queues and APIs.

### Mitigation

* Redeployment of services to free up resources
* Actions to unblock queued up events
* A hotfix was deployed to optimize an identified complex query and reduce system strain.

### Next Steps

To prevent similar issues we are working on improvements for:

* Query handling for stopped messages will be further optimized.
* Enhanced monitoring and tooling around internal message handling usage and query execution are being introduced.

We appreciate your patience and understanding, and apologize for any inconvenience. Please reach out if you have any questions or need further clarification.

incidents.body:
**Summary**  
On August 20th, we experienced an issue affecting connectivity and performance in our API Gateway. The incident was identified and resolved within a short time frame.  
  
**Customer impact**  
During the incident, some customers experienced degraded performance and intermittent connectivity issues when accessing the API Gateway. Other platform functionality remained unaffected.  
  
**Root cause**  
The issue was caused by an SSL certificate deployment that introduced unexpected connectivity and performance problems.  
  
**Mitigation**  
Once identified, the deployment was quickly reverted, which immediately stabilized the platform. A permanent fix has since been implemented, and no further performance degradation has been observed.  
  
**Next steps**  
We have updated our deployment routines and processes to ensure similar issues are avoided in the future.
incidents.title: [Engage] Service Disruption

incidents.body:
## Summary

On August 19th, Voyado Engage experienced degraded performance on the Contact API due to an issue introduced in a recent release.

## Customer Impact

Customers using the Contact API may have experienced slower response times. Other parts of the platform remained fully operational.

## Root Cause

A code change led to unintended system behavior that affected backend performance. The issue was related to a specific component used to detect changes in contact data.

## Mitigation

The problematic code was disabled through a targeted hotfix, which restored normal performance.

## Next steps

We are improving safeguards around this component and enhancing our deployment checks to prevent similar issues in the future.

We are sorry for the disruption this caused and appreciate your patience while we worked to resolve the issue.
